themes.title: AI fundamentals
themes.intro: Understand what a model does, how it learns, and what its performance measures mean.

papers.title: AI for Radiology: A Primer Part I. From Idea to Algorithm
papers.citation: Tejani AS, Rauschecker AM, Kohli M, Mongan J. Radiology. 2025;317(1):e250692.
papers.description: An introduction to AI development, including data curation, annotation, training and testing, and evaluation.

papers.title: AI for Radiology: A Primer Part II. Interacting with AI Results
papers.citation: Tejani AS, Kohli M, Rauschecker AM, et al. Radiology. 2026;320(1):e252702.
papers.description: Explains how AI results are generated, presented, and documented, and how those choices affect radiologists’ workflows.

papers.title: Evaluation metrics in medical imaging AI: fundamentals, pitfalls, misapplications, and recommendations
papers.citation: Kocak B, Klontzas ME, Stanzione A, et al. European Journal of Radiology Artificial Intelligence. 2025;3:100030.
papers.description: A reference for task-specific metrics, calibration, statistical comparison, and common evaluation pitfalls, including generative AI.

papers.title: Foundation Models in Radiology: What, How, Why, and Why Not
papers.citation: Paschali M, Chen Z, Blankemeier L, et al. Radiology. 2025;314(2):e240597.
papers.description: Introduces foundation models, including their training and adaptation, capabilities, evaluation, and limitations in radiology.

papers.title: Uncover This Tech Term: Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Radiology
papers.citation: Faghani S, Moassefi M, Rouzrokh P, Khosravi B, Erickson BJ. Korean Journal of Radiology. 2025;26(9):888–892.
papers.description: Explains AI agents, their relationship to foundation models, and how planning, tool use, and observation enable multistep workflows.

themes.title: Radiology AI use cases
themes.intro: Connect AI capabilities to the clinical and operational problems you want to solve.

papers.title: Radiology Workflow Assistance With Artificial Intelligence: Establishing the Link to Outcomes
papers.citation: Gu Z, Dogra S, Siriruchatanon M, Kneifati-Hayek J, Kang SK. Journal of the American College of Radiology. 2026;23(3):389–398.
papers.description: Reviews AI applications across the imaging workflow, their performance measures, and the evidence connecting workflow gains to downstream outcomes.

papers.title: Chatbots and Large Language Models in Radiology: A Practical Primer for Clinical and Research Applications
papers.description: Reviews clinical and research applications of language models, including protocoling, reporting, information extraction, and patient communication, alongside their limitations.

themes.title: Biases affecting AI
themes.intro: Assess the data, study design, and patient populations behind reported results.

papers.title: Understanding and Mitigating Bias in Imaging Artificial Intelligence
papers.citation: Tejani AS, Ng YS, Xi Y, Rayan JC. RadioGraphics. 2024;44(5):e230067.
papers.description: An overview of bias across the imaging AI life cycle, including data representation, labeling, leakage, subgroup performance, and distribution shift.

papers.title: Detecting Common Sources of AI Bias: Questions to Ask When Procuring an AI Solution
papers.citation: Tejani AS, Retson TA, Moy L, Cook TS. Radiology. 2023;307(3):e230580.
papers.description: Practical questions for assessing training populations, labeling, model evaluation, distribution shift, and bias before acquiring an AI tool.

themes.title: AI effect on radiologists
themes.intro: Consider how AI influences interpretation, trust, and clinical decisions.

papers.title: Human–AI interaction and collaboration in radiology: from conceptual frameworks to responsible implementation
papers.citation: Kocak B, Cuocolo R. Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology. 2026;32(5):535–547.
papers.description: A narrative review of human–AI collaboration, automation bias, algorithmic aversion, deskilling, workload, and practical implementation in radiology.

themes.title: Real-world AI evaluation
themes.intro: Evaluate clinical value and workflow impact, and plan for ongoing monitoring.

papers.title: Developing, Purchasing, Implementing and Monitoring AI Tools in Radiology: Practical Considerations
papers.citation: Brady AP, Allen B, Chong J, et al. Radiology: Artificial Intelligence. 2024;6(1):e230513. Multisociety statement from the ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, and RSNA.
papers.description: Guidance on clinical value, meaningful outcomes, local evaluation, workflow integration, costs and benefits, and ongoing monitoring.

papers.title: Postdeployment Monitoring and Surveillance Methods, Guidelines, and Possibilities for AI in Radiology
papers.citation: Venugopal VK, Khubchandani SA, Liew CJY, et al. RadioGraphics. 2026;46(7):e250173.
papers.description: Reviews monitoring approaches for input and output drift, uncertainty, alert thresholds, escalation, and investigation of performance problems after deployment.

themes.title: Regulatory and ethical considerations
themes.intro: Recognize the regulatory, legal, and ethical questions surrounding AI use.

papers.title: FDA Review of Radiologic AI Algorithms: Process and Challenges
papers.citation: Zhang K, Khosravi B, Vahdati S, Erickson BJ. Radiology. 2024;310(1):e230242.
papers.description: Explains FDA review of imaging AI algorithms as software medical devices and discusses clinical implementation challenges following clearance.

papers.title: Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Summary of the Joint European and North American Multisociety Statement
papers.citation: Geis JR, Brady AP, Wu CC, et al. Radiology. 2019;293(2):436–440.
papers.description: A foundational consensus statement on privacy, fairness, transparency, patient benefit, and human accountability in radiology AI.

papers.title: Understanding Liability Risk from Using Health Care Artificial Intelligence Tools
papers.citation: Mello MM, Guha N. New England Journal of Medicine. 2024;390(3):271–278.
papers.description: Reviews AI-related malpractice and software-error liability, with risk-management considerations for clinicians and healthcare organizations.
